concept.name: Slippage model
concept.definition: A model of the difference between a decision or reference price and the simulated execution price attributable to spread, delay, liquidity, and impact.
concept.intuition: It is part of the machinery that converts strategy instructions into simulated positions, cash flows, and performance.
concept.mechanics: Estimate an adverse price adjustment from order size, volume, volatility, latency, or a calibrated constant and apply it to the fill price.
concept.failure_modes: Simplified timing, liquidity, fee, borrow, funding, or corporate-action assumptions can make simulated results unattainable live.
concept.misconceptions: A detailed simulator reduces modeling error but cannot reproduce every queue event or future market condition.
concept.example: A buy order with 8 basis points of modeled slippage fills at 100.08 when the reference price is 100.
